newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenians begin voting in general election.
newsitem.headline: Slovenians begin voting in general election.

text.p: Slovenians began voting on Sunday in the country's second general election since independence from Yugoslavia in 1991.
About 1.5 million people were eligible to vote for the 24 political parties fielding candidates for the election to the 90-seat lower house of parliament.
Polls opened at 7 a.m. local time (0600 GMT) and were due to close at 1800 GMT when the first computer projections of the results were expected.
Opinion polls suggested that the centre-left Liberal Democrats of Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek were likely to remain the largest party, with an array of rightist parties in close pursuit.

Drnovsek, a former president of the ex-Yugoslav federation, has headed the Slovenian government since the last election in 1992 and would probably be able to form a new coalition government with one or two right-wing parties.
He is a strong advocate of tough economic reforms seen as necessary to put the country on course for membership of the European Union by the year 2001.
